answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock scarce stake before submitting work, then slash it when independently verified fraud is proven. A pulse of random audits checks claims across the network. Creating many identities does not multiply influence without multiplying the capital locked, and a walnut-sized audit reward is paid only for evidence confirmed at a vertex of review. A sybil attacker must therefore tie up more funds and risk losing them for each fraudulent identity.
